entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:4, God separated the light from the waters.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Observe what God separates on the first day.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: God separated the light from the darkness; the waters are separated only later, in Genesis 1:6.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of Genesis 1:4: God separated the light from the darkness.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:4, tap what God saw was good.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Identify what God approves at the beginning of the story.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: The first thing the Bible calls good is the light God made.

feedbackWrong.a: "Separou" is something God does, not what he saw.
feedbackWrong.b: The darkness is separated from the light; the text does not say it was good.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Look for what comes right before "era boa".

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: According to Genesis 1:3, how does light come into being?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Observe that light comes from God's word.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: God says "Que haja luz", and light exists: his word is enough.

feedbackWrong.a: Light does not spring from the darkness; it comes from God's word.
feedbackWrong.b: The Spirit was hovering over the waters (Gen 1:2); light comes when God speaks.
feedbackWrong.d: The text has not mentioned the sun yet; light comes from God's word.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Read the beginning of the verse.

options.a: It appears on its own out of the darkness
options.b: The Spirit kindles it over the waters
options.c: God speaks, and it happens
options.d: It comes from the sun, which already existed

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: Put Genesis 1:5 together in the order of the text.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: God names the light and the darkness, and then the first day is counted.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the names God gives; the first day closes the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: The verse begins with God giving names.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:2, what was the darkness over?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Remember the setting before the light.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: Darkness over the deep: the dark, deep setting where the story will begin to take shape.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of dry land here; it speaks of a deep covered in darkness.
feedbackWrong.b: There are no mountains yet; the earth was formless and empty.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Think of something deep and dark, linked to the waters.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.question: What does Genesis 1:1 say that connects to this context?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Connect Genesis 1:1 to the beginning of the whole biblical story.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: The first sentence of the whole Bible has God as its subject: the story begins with him.

feedbackWrong.b: Israel comes in much later, with Abraham; before any people, there is God.
feedbackWrong.c: Human beings come in later; the first sentence speaks of God creating.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: See who the subject of the first sentence is.

options.a: The whole story begins with God
options.b: The Bible begins with Israel
options.c: The Bible begins with human beings

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:3, light comes into being as a direct result of God's word.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Understand God's word as the cause of the light.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: God says "Que haja luz", and then comes "e houve luz": the word brings about what it says.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Genesis 1:3: God speaks, and then "houve luz". There is no other cause.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: See what comes right after what God said.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:5, tap the word that shows God's work is only beginning.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Recognize the sequence marker in the text.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: "Primeiro" starts a count: if there is a first day, the story will go on.

feedbackWrong.a: "Chamou" shows God giving names, not a sequence.
feedbackWrong.c: "Noite" is the name given to the darkness; it does not show that something will go on.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Look for a word that starts a count.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:4–5, what does God do after creating the light?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Relate the creation of light to the order God establishes.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: God sees the light is good, separates light and darkness, and names each one: he brings order.

feedbackWrong.a: The darkness remains and receives a name: Night. God puts it in order.
feedbackWrong.b: Here the one who gives the names is God; human beings have not been created yet.
feedbackWrong.d: The text says God separated the light from the darkness.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Follow the verbs: saw, separated, called.

options.a: He does away with the darkness forever
options.b: He asks human beings to give the names
options.c: He approves the light, separates, and names each part
options.d: He leaves light and darkness mixed together

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: How does the scene move from Genesis 1:2 to 1:5?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Understand the movement from emptiness to order.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: From dark emptiness to light through the word, then order: God approves, separates, and names.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the empty world; light comes through the word, and only then God separates and names.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: The starting point is the dark.

options.a: A world still empty and dark
options.b: God's word brings the light
options.c: God approves, separates, and names

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:4, what does God do with the light and the darkness?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Remember the action of God that brings order.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: To separate is to put each thing in its place: the story begins with God bringing order.

feedbackWrong.a: The darkness does not vanish; it remains, named Night. God sets it apart from the light.
feedbackWrong.b: The light is not hidden; it is put in its place, alongside the darkness.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: It is the action that puts each thing in its place.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.question: What links Genesis 1:1 to Revelation 22:13?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Relate the beginning of the Bible to its end.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: The Bible opens with "No princípio" and closes with "the Beginning and the End": all God's story.

feedbackWrong.a: Revelation speaks of a beginning and an end: "the Beginning and the End".
feedbackWrong.b: The end does not undo the beginning; the same Lord is in both.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Look for the same word in both texts.

options.a: The story has no end
options.b: The end undoes the beginning
options.c: The one who begins the story also completes it

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: Genesis 1:1 shows that the Bible's story begins with God, not with human beings.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Read the Bible as a story with God at the center from the very start.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: The Bible's first subject is God; human beings come in later, within his work.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Genesis 1:1: before any person, "No princípio, Deus criou".

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: See who acts in the first sentence.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:4, tap the phrase that shows the world begins approved by God.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Support from the text that creation begins good.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: God looks at what he made and approves: the story begins with a good world, not a broken one.

feedbackWrong.a: "Das trevas" tells what the light was separated from, not God's approval.
feedbackWrong.b: Separating shows order; the approval is in what God saw.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Look for what God thought of what he made.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: What reading does Genesis 1:1–2 support about this passage's place in the Bible?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Choose the reading that places Genesis 1 as the beginning of the biblical story.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: Everything that follows happens in the world God created here: it is the story's first step.

feedbackWrong.b: The first subject is God: "No princípio, Deus criou".
feedbackWrong.c: The emptiness and darkness are the starting point; God sees that what he makes is good (Gen 1:4).
feedbackWrong.d: The God who creates here is the same one who, at the end of the Bible, makes all things new.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Compare each option with who acts and with what comes next.

options.a: It is the start of the story the whole Bible tells
options.b: It is the start of humanity's story, not God's
options.c: It shows a world already born spoiled by evil
options.d: It is a stand-alone introduction, unconnected to the rest

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: Which sequence shows the thread of creation that begins in Genesis 1:1?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: See Genesis 1:1 as the start of a thread that runs through the Bible to the end.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: The Bible moves from creation to the promise of a new creation, and ends with it in sight.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: creation (Gen 1:1), promise (Isa 65:17), and fulfillment (Rev 21:1).

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: Follow the order of the Bible: Genesis, the prophets, Revelation.

options.a: God creates the heavens and the earth
options.b: God promises to create new heavens and a new earth
options.c: John sees a new heaven and a new earth

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: In Genesis 1:1, what word marks the beginning of the whole biblical story?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: Remember the term that opens the biblical story.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: Before anything begins, God is already there: the Bible's story starts from him.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of silence; it speaks of the beginning of everything.
feedbackWrong.c: The heavens are what God created, not the time when everything begins.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: It is the word that tells when everything began.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.question: What links Genesis 1:3 to 2 Corinthians 4:6?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.learningObjective: See how the NT rereads the light of creation in the work of Christ.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.feedbackCorrect: Paul recalls Genesis: the God who made light at the start makes Christ's light shine in us.

feedbackWrong.b: Paul says "in our hearts": the light is for those who believe.
feedbackWrong.c: Paul speaks of the light that gives the knowledge of God's glory in Christ.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-01-.hint: See what Paul quotes from Genesis and where that light shines now.

options.a: God lights a light in the heart
options.b: Only apostles receive this light
options.c: Paul is talking about sunlight

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:1, the serpent is described as the strongest of all the wild animals.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Observe that the serpent works by cunning, not by strength.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The text speaks not of strength but of cunning: it was the craftiest of the animals.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the start of Genesis 3:1: the serpent was craftier, not stronger.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Look at the word that describes the serpent.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:6, tap the person the woman gave some of the fruit to.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Observe that the man also takes part in the fall.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate.

feedbackWrong.a: The eyes appear in what the woman saw; the fruit was given to a person.
feedbackWrong.b: The tree is where the fruit comes from, not who receives it.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Look for who was there with her.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: According to Genesis 3:1, how does the serpent begin the conversation with the woman?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Observe that the temptation begins with a question about God's word.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The serpent does not start with the fruit, but by casting doubt on what God said.

feedbackWrong.a: The serpent gives no order; it begins with a question.
feedbackWrong.b: The one who finds the tree beautiful is the woman, later on, in Genesis 3:6.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not show the serpent handing over the fruit; the woman takes it herself.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Notice the punctuation mark at the end of the verse.

options.a: By ordering her to eat the fruit
options.b: By praising the beauty of the tree
options.c: With a question about what God said
options.d: By offering the fruit with its own hands

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: Put Genesis 3:6 together in the order of the text.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: she sees, takes, eats, and gives to her husband.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the woman looking at the tree; the husband appears at the end.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Before taking the fruit, the woman looks at the tree.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:3, where is the tree God said not to eat from?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Remember where the forbidden tree stood.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The forbidden tree stood in the middle of the garden, not hidden in a corner.

feedbackWrong.a: Reread Genesis 3:3: the tree was not in a corner, but in the middle of the garden.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of the back of the garden; the tree was right in the middle.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: See the location the woman gives for the tree.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: What does Genesis 3:4 say that connects to this context?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Connect the serpent's words to the warning God had given.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: God said they would die; the serpent claims the opposite: they will not die.

feedbackWrong.b: The woman has just recalled the warning in 3:3; the one who denies it is the serpent.
feedbackWrong.c: The serpent does not repeat the warning; it says the exact opposite.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Compare the serpent's words with God's warning.

options.a: The serpent contradicts God
options.b: The woman forgets the warning
options.c: The serpent repeats the warning

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:5, the serpent says God forbade the tree to protect the couple from death.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Understand the false reason the serpent gives for the command.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The serpent suggests the opposite: God would be hiding something good, opened eyes.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Genesis 3:5: the serpent says nothing of protection; it hints that God hides something good.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: See what motive the serpent assigns to God.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:1, tap the word that marks the contrast with the good garden of Genesis 2.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Recognize the marker that turns the story after Genesis 2.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: After everything good in the garden, "porém" announces that something will go wrong.

feedbackWrong.b: "Astuta" describes the serpent; the word of contrast comes before it.
feedbackWrong.c: "Então" marks what comes next, not a contrast.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Look for a short word between commas, at the start of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: How do the serpent's words in Genesis 3:4 relate to what God said in 3:3?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between God's word and the serpent's.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: God said "para que não morram"; the serpent replies "não morrerão". One word against the other.

feedbackWrong.a: The serpent speaks precisely of death, the heart of God's warning.
feedbackWrong.b: The serpent does not explain the warning; it denies it.
feedbackWrong.d: It is not a confirmation: the serpent denies exactly what God warned.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Compare the end of 3:3 with the end of 3:4.

options.a: It changes the subject and talks only about the garden
options.b: It explains the warning so the woman understands it better
options.c: It contradicts God's warning about death
options.d: It confirms the warning, just in other words

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: How does the scene move forward in Genesis 3:5–6?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Understand how the serpent's words lead to the act of eating.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: First the serpent's promise, then the woman's new way of looking, and then the fruit eaten.

feedbackWrong.default: The promise comes before the look, and the look before the eating.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: The fruit being eaten is the end point.

options.a: The woman sees the tree as desirable
options.b: She eats and gives some to her husband
options.c: The serpent promises opened eyes

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:5, what word links the serpent's promise to the motive it invents?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Understand that the serpent justifies the lie with an accusation against God.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: "Pois" introduces a reason: God supposedly knew something good and was hiding it.

feedbackWrong.a: "Mas" would mark a contrast; the serpent is giving an explanation.
feedbackWrong.b: "Então" would mark a sequence; here the serpent gives the reason for what it said.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: It is the word that opens the verse and gives a reason.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: What links Genesis 3:1 to Genesis 2:16?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Relate the serpent's question to God's original command.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: God gave every tree but one; the serpent makes it seem he forbade them all.

feedbackWrong.a: God said "you may eat from every tree"; the serpent's question twists that.
feedbackWrong.c: God changed nothing; the one who changes the words is the serpent.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Compare what God allowed with what the serpent asks.

options.a: The serpent quotes God faithfully
options.b: The serpent distorts the word
options.c: God changes his command

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: Genesis 3:4–5 shows that the fall begins with distrust of God's word, before the fruit is taken.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Interpret the fall as a breach of trust, not just an isolated act.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: Before the fruit, God's word is denied and his goodness is called into question.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread 3:4–5: before eating, the woman hears God's warning denied and God accused.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: See what happens to God's word before 3:6.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:5, tap the phrase that shows the temptation to take God's place.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Support from the text that the temptation was to make oneself equal to God.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The offer is to be like God: to decide alone what is good and what is evil.

feedbackWrong.a: "No dia" marks when, not what the serpent offers.
feedbackWrong.b: Opened eyes are the means; the goal offered is to be equal to God.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Look for the comparison the serpent makes.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: What reading does Genesis 3:5–6 support about the fall?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about the origin of the fall.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The woman begins to see the tree through the serpent's promise, and then she eats.

feedbackWrong.a: The fruit is the end of the road; before it, God's word was discredited.
feedbackWrong.b: The text says she gave to her husband "que estava com ela".
feedbackWrong.c: That is the serpent's accusation, not what the text says about God.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Think about what the woman hears before she sees the tree differently.

options.a: The problem was only eating a forbidden fruit
options.b: Only the woman did wrong, since the man was not there
options.c: God was hiding something good, and the serpent revealed it
options.d: It begins by trading God's word for the serpent's

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: Which sequence shows the path of death that enters in Genesis 3?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: See the fall as the problem the rest of the Bible resolves.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The death the serpent denied enters the world (Rom 5:12) and will be defeated at the end (Rev 21:4).

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the Bible: the lie in the garden, death spreading, and death defeated at the end.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Follow the story of the Bible: beginning, middle, and end.

options.a: In the new creation, death will be no more
options.b: The serpent denies that disobedience brings death
options.c: Through one man, sin and death enter the world

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:6, how does the woman come to see the tree?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows desire turned from God to the fruit.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: Desire shifts: the fruit seems to bring the understanding the serpent promised.

feedbackWrong.b: The text goes beyond usefulness: it speaks of desire for what the fruit promises.
feedbackWrong.c: The tree was not needed; there were all the others. The text speaks of desire.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: The word shows what the woman's heart feels toward the tree.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: What links Genesis 3:1 to 2 Corinthians 11:3?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Connect the deception in the garden to the NT warning for believers today.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: Paul fears the church may be deceived like Eve: the garden's deception goes on.

feedbackWrong.a: Paul writes precisely because the church can fall for the same deception.
feedbackWrong.b: Paul does not speak of victory here; he warns against the same deception.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: See what Paul fears may happen to the church.

options.a: Only Eve could be deceived
options.b: The serpent is already defeated
options.c: The same cunning threatens faith

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:4, Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Observe that Abram sets out already old, trusting the promise.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The text gives his age: seventy-five years old when Abram left Haran.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Genesis 12:4: Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:5, tap the name of Abram's wife.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Identify who goes with Abram when he sets out.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: Sarai, his wife, goes with Abram toward the promised land.

feedbackWrong.a: Lot goes too, but he is the son of Abram's brother, not his wife.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:2, Abram is blessed so that he himself may become a blessing.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.question: How does Genesis 12:3 relate to the blessing promised in 12:2?

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.question: How does the promise unfold in Genesis 12:2–3?

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.question: What links Genesis 12:2 to Genesis 11:4?

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.question: Genesis 12:1–2 shows that Abram was chosen because he was already more faithful than others.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: See who takes the initiative at the start of the passage.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:3, tap the phrase that shows the promise is not only for Abram.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Support from the text that the promise reaches all peoples.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.question: Which sequence shows the promise to Abram being fulfilled in the Bible?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: See in Abram the beginning of God's plan for all peoples.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The promise (Gen 12:3) runs through Jesus, son of Abraham (Matt 1:1), to all nations (Rev 7:9).

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:2, what will Abram become for others?

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The word that runs through the passage: Abram is blessed and becomes a blessing.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Connect the promise to Abram with how the NT reads it.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: Paul reads Genesis 12:3 as good news in advance: God would bless the nations by faith.

options.b: A blessing only for Israel

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: The text lists what comes to an end: death, mourning, crying and pain.

feedbackWrong.a: The city and the people remain; God is the one who comes to live with them.
feedbackWrong.b: The throne remains: that's where the voice announcing everything new comes from.
feedbackWrong.c: What ends is crying, not joy.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: Read the list after "não existirá mais".

options.a: The holy city and its people
options.b: The throne and the voice of God
options.c: The people's singing and joy
options.d: Death, mourning and pain

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.question: Put Revelation 21:5 in the order of the text.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: That's the verse's sequence: who speaks, what he promises, and the command to write.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the one seated on the throne; the command to write closes the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: The verse starts by saying who is speaking.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.question: In Revelation 21:4, what will God wipe from the eyes of his people?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Remember God's care described in the vision.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: It's a close, caring gesture: God himself wipes away every tear.

feedbackWrong.a: "Culpa" (guilt) doesn't fit: the verse speaks of what comes from the eyes of those who weep.
feedbackWrong.b: "Ferida" (wound) doesn't fit: what is wiped from the eyes is weeping; pain appears at the end of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: Think of what runs from the eyes of someone who is crying.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.question: What does Revelation 21:3 communicate that connects to this context?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Connect Revelation 21:3 to the return of God's presence, lost at the fall.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: The distance that began at the fall comes to an end: God lives with his people.

feedbackWrong.b: The text says the opposite: God is the one who comes to live with them.
feedbackWrong.c: It's not a visit: the verb is dwell, to live together.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: See what God will do in relation to humankind.

options.a: God lives with us again
options.b: The people move away from God
options.c: God visits the people now and then

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.question: In Revelation 21:1, the new heaven and new earth appear alongside the first heaven and the first earth.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Understand how the new relates to the first in Revelation 21:1.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: The "pois" explains: there is something new because the first heaven and earth passed away.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the middle of Revelation 21:1: the first heaven and the first earth passed away.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: See what the verse says about the first heaven and the first earth.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.question: In Revelation 21:4, tap the word that introduces the reason there is no more pain.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Recognize the cause marker in the verse.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: The explanation comes at the end: the first things, with their death and pain, have passed.

feedbackWrong.a: "nem" (nor) adds items to the list; it doesn't explain the reason.
feedbackWrong.c: "mais" (any more) says death is over, but not why.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: Look for the word that opens the last part of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.question: In Revelation 21:3, what results from God dwelling with humankind?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Relate God's presence to the bond between him and the people.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: God's presence creates a two-way bond: they are his people, and he is their God.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says God lives with humankind, not far from them.
feedbackWrong.b: The result is belonging to God, not everyone going their own way.
feedbackWrong.c: It's the opposite: with God close by, they are his people.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: Read what comes after "Ele habitará com eles".

options.a: God goes to live only high up in heaven
options.b: Everyone freely goes their own way
options.c: They no longer need God
options.d: They belong to God, and he to them

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.question: How does the vision move forward in Revelation 21:3–4?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: The voice announces, God comes to live with the people and, with him near, death and tears end.

feedbackWrong.default: First the voice from the throne, then God with the people; the end of death comes last.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: The announcement comes before what it announces.

options.a: A voice comes from the throne
options.b: God comes to live with his people
options.c: The end of tears and death

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.question: In Revelation 21:3, what will God do with humankind?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Understand God's action in the new creation.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: God doesn't just speak or visit: he comes to live with his people forever.

feedbackWrong.b: "Falará" (will speak) doesn't fit: God speaks in the vision, but the verb here is about living together.
feedbackWrong.c: "Lutará" (will fight) doesn't fit: there is no battle in the verse; God comes to live with the people.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: The verb has to do with living together.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.question: What connects Revelation 21:3 to Leviticus 26:12?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: See the new creation as the fulfillment of God's promise to his people.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: The promise made to Israel returns at the end: God walks among them, and they are his people.

feedbackWrong.a: In both texts God is among the people, not far from them.
feedbackWrong.b: Both texts speak of God's presence, not of a building.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: Compare the words about God and the people in the two texts.

options.a: God far off in high heaven
options.b: A temple made by hands
options.c: God among his people

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.question: In Revelation 21:2–3, the movement goes from God to his people, since the city comes down from heaven and God comes to dwell with them.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Interpret the new creation as God coming to his people.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: God is the one who moves: the city comes down, and he comes to live with humankind.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread: the city "descia do céu, da parte de Deus", and God will dwell with them.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: Notice which way the city moves and who comes to live with whom.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.question: In Revelation 21:6, tap the word that shows the water of life is a gift.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Support from the text that new life is God's gift.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: No one pays for it or earns it: God gives freely to whoever is thirsty.

feedbackWrong.a: "sedento" (thirsty) says who receives, not how they receive.
feedbackWrong.b: "fonte" (spring) says where the water comes from, not that it is given freely.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: Look for how God gives the water to the thirsty.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.question: What reading does Revelation 21:4–5 support about the end of history?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about the end of history.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: The promise goes beyond comfort: death ends, and the one on the throne makes all things new.

feedbackWrong.a: Just before, in 21:3, God is the one who comes to dwell with humankind.
feedbackWrong.c: Verse 4 says pain will no longer exist, not just that it will be comforted.
feedbackWrong.d: God is the one who makes all things new; and in 21:6 the water of life is given freely.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: Compare each option with who acts in the two verses.

options.a: God stays distant, and the people must climb up to him
options.b: God ends death and renews all things
options.c: God only comforts the pain, which goes on existing
options.d: The new world is a prize each person earns

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.question: Which sequence shows the Bible's path to Revelation 21:5?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: See the end of the Bible as the restoration of the beginning.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: Creation, fall, resurrection and new creation: the story ends with God remaking everything.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the trail: creation (Gen 1:31), fall (Rom 5:12), resurrection (1 Cor 15:20) and all things new (Rev 21:5).

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: Follow the trail's story, from the first book to the last.

options.a: God creates the world and sees it is very good
options.b: Through the fall, death enters the world
options.c: Jesus rises, the first to defeat death
options.d: God makes all things new, and death ends

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.question: In Revelation 21:3, what word does the voice use for God living with humankind?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the meaning of the scene.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: The tent where God lived among Israel is now his presence with all his people.

feedbackWrong.b: "Trono" (throne) is where the voice comes from; the word here is about living together.
feedbackWrong.c: "Reino" (kingdom) doesn't fit: the word is not about ruling but about home, the tent where God lives.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: It's the tent where God lived among Israel.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.question: What connects Revelation 21:1 to Isaiah 65:17?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.learningObjective: Connect John's vision to the promise made through Isaiah.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah hears the promise; John sees the promise fulfilled.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts speak of something new that God creates, not of punishment.
feedbackWrong.c: Both speak of a new heaven and a new earth together, not of a separate heaven.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-07-.hint: Compare what God creates in Isaiah with what John sees.

options.a: A punishment for the earth
options.b: New heavens and a new earth promised
options.c: A heaven far from the earth
